vetting_gates.name: Eclipse count
vetting_gates.text: At least the minimum number of eclipses required to trust a period, so a single noisy dip can never pass on its own.

vetting_gates.name: Odd/even depth consistency
vetting_gates.text: Alternating eclipses must be statistically consistent in depth. A significant odd/even split is often the signature of an undetected period alias rather than two different eclipse depths.

vetting_gates.name: Robust detection significance
vetting_gates.text: The in-eclipse dip must clear a signal-to-noise threshold computed with an outlier-robust noise estimate, not a plain standard deviation that outliers could inflate.

vetting_gates.name: Secondary eclipse search
vetting_gates.text: The phase-folded curve is searched for a secondary eclipse independent of the primary detection, informing the tier and caveats even when none is required to pass.

vetting_gates.name: BLS signal-to-noise
vetting_gates.text: The Box Least Squares periodogram signal-to-noise ratio must clear a minimum threshold for the detected period to be trusted.

pixel_gates.name: In-eclipse light curve dip
pixel_gates.text: The dip must independently reappear at the same phase in this sector's own light curve, at significance.

pixel_gates.name: Difference-image peak SNR
pixel_gates.text: The out-of-eclipse minus in-eclipse pixel difference image must show a significant, spatially compact source, not scattered noise.

pixel_gates.name: Epoch-shift consistency
pixel_gates.text: The eclipse timing recovered independently at the pixel level must line up with the light-curve ephemeris, ruling out an unrelated nearby variable aligning by chance.

pixel_gates.name: Source compactness
pixel_gates.text: The difference-image source must be consistent with a single point spread function, not a diffuse or multi-peaked pattern that would suggest blended light.

pixel_gates.name: Centroid offset
pixel_gates.text: The photometric centroid shift between in- and out-of-eclipse images must stay within the target's own pixel, or the signal is charged to a neighbour instead.

pixel_gates.name: Nearest-neighbour contamination
pixel_gates.text: Catalog neighbours within the aperture are checked by brightness and distance, so a bright nearby star cannot masquerade as the target dimming.
